premises: Oxygen contamination in HfNbTaTiZr forms defect clusters that alter electronic structure and carrier scattering.
Ab initio calculations on small clusters can accurately capture defect levels and local band perturbations from oxygen.
These ab initio results can be parameterized into an empirical potential model to simulate bulk transport.
At low temperatures (0–200 K), conduction occurs via hopping between localized states associated with oxygen defect clusters.
At high temperatures (300–1200 K), thermal excitation from defect states to extended states yields intrinsic conduction modified by the defect landscape.
